contents.text: VizRelationshipCoverage shows unmatched PK values in the Customers dimension, customers that don't appear in any invoice. How many are there, and which customers are they?

<toolcall tool="execute_dax_query" id="call_bBfCaYXq7dErG6cY3uIbNrkw" display="Executing DAX query" details="EVALUATE
VAR UnmatchedCustomers =
    EXCEPT(
        VALUES(Customers[Customer Key]),
        VALUES(Invoices[Customer Key])
    )
RETURN
    ADDCOLUMNS(
        UnmatchedCustomers,
        "Customer Sold-To Name", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Customer Sold-To Name])),
        "Account Name", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Account Name])),
        "Key Account Name", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Key Account Name])),
        "Account Type", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Account Type])),
        "Transaction Type", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Transaction Type]))
    )
ORDER BY [Customer Key]" done="true"/>There are **23** unmatched customers in [Customers](te3://objref/Customers) — customer keys that do not appear in [Invoices](te3://objref/Invoices).

If you want, I can also split these into:
- customers with **zero invoices but present in Budget**
- customers with **no fact-table activity at all**
- customers grouped by **Account Type** or **Key Account**.
Is there a pattern in these customers vs the other customers?

<toolcall tool="execute_dax_query" id="call_toGC2aiFl9cxpcK7mdDL3uXl" display="Executing DAX query" details="EVALUATE
VAR UnmatchedCustomers =
    FILTER(
        ADDCOLUMNS(
            VALUES(Customers[Customer Key]),
            "InvoiceCount", CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(Invoices)),
            "OrderCount", CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(Orders)),
            "BudgetCount", CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(Budget)),
            "AccountType", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Account Type])),
            "TransactionType", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Transaction Type])),
            "Station", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Station])),
            "AccountName", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Account Name])),
            "SoldToName", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Customer Sold-To Name])),
            "KeyAccountName", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Key Account Name]))
        ),
        [InvoiceCount] = 0
    )
RETURN
    SUMMARIZECOLUMNS(
        UnmatchedCustomers[AccountType],
        UnmatchedCustomers[TransactionType],
        "Customers", COUNTROWS(UnmatchedCustomers),
        "With Orders", COUNTROWS(FILTER(UnmatchedCustomers, [OrderCount] > 0)),
        "With Budget", COUNTROWS(FILTER(UnmatchedCustomers, [BudgetCount] > 0))
    )" failed="true"/><toolcall tool="execute_dax_query" id="call_LRd2ny0P4DzZ37GIsANdhDci" display="Executing DAX query" details="EVALUATE
VAR UnmatchedCustomers =
    FILTER(
        ADDCOLUMNS(
            VALUES(Customers[Customer Key]),
            "InvoiceCount", CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(Invoices)),
            "OrderCount", CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(Orders)),
            "BudgetCount", CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(Budget)),
            "AccountType", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Account Type])),
            "TransactionType", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Transaction Type])),
            "Station", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Station])),
            "AccountName", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Account Name])),
            "SoldToName", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Customer Sold-To Name])),
            "KeyAccountName", CALCULATE(SELECTEDVALUE(Customers[Key Account Name]))
        ),
        [InvoiceCount] = 0
    )
RETURN
    SELECTCOLUMNS(
        UnmatchedCustomers,
        "Customer Key", Customers[Customer Key],
        "Account Type", [AccountType],
        "Transaction Type", [TransactionType],
        "Orders", [OrderCount],
        "Budget", [BudgetCount],
        "Station", [Station],
        "Account Name", [AccountName],
        "Sold-To", [SoldToName],
        "Key Account Name", [KeyAccountName]
    )
ORDER BY [Account Type], [Transaction Type], [Customer Key]" done="true"/>Yes. A few clear patterns in the unmatched [Customers](te3://objref/Customers) that have no [Invoices](te3://objref/Invoices):

- They are all still present in [Orders](te3://objref/Orders). So these are not dead dimension members; they’re just invoice-less. Very on-brand for a model with a dramatic relationship coverage issue.
- They split cleanly by [Account Type](te3://objref/Customers[Account Type]):
  - **9** `Key Account`
  - **11** `No Key Account`
  - **3** `Private Buyer`
- The `Key Account` ones are mostly branch-level customers tied to a shared parent account in [Key Account Name](te3://objref/Customers[Key Account Name]) and [Account Name](te3://objref/Customers[Account Name]) — for example:
  - [Aminu Kano Navy](te3://objref/Customers[Account Name]) appears in multiple branches
  - [Black Flag Spaceships](te3://objref/Customers[Account Name]) appears in multiple branches
  - [Supernova Spaceparts](te3://objref/Customers[Account Name]) appears once
- The `No Key Account` customers are mostly standalone B2B accounts with no invoice activity.
- The `Private Buyer` customers are all B2C records with `Transaction Type = B2C` and `Key Account Name = Private Contract`.

So the pattern is less “mysterious orphan” and more:
1. all have orders,
2. none have invoices,
3. they cluster by customer type, with branch-style key accounts being the most common.

If you want, I can also break this down by:
- [Station](te3://objref/Customers[Station])
- [Account Type](te3://objref/Customers[Account Type])
- whether they have **Budget** rows as well
- or identify which of these are likely data quality issues vs legitimate pre-invoice customers.
